pose_prompt_base: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: simplyZOMBIES static pixel-art pose sheet for visual review and later sprite extraction. Input image 1 is the approved shambler; image 2 is the approved survivor. Match their compact chunky proportions, large simple head, short legs, dark stepped outer contour, muted palette and broad readable pixel clusters. Artwork should read at roughly 32 by 40 native pixels per standing figure, displayed enlarged; three or four flat shades per material, light from upper left, no photoreal miniature texture. Exactly THREE isolated poses of the SAME zombie in a single horizontal row on true RGBA transparency with wide empty gutters. LEFT: living standing south-facing three-quarter elevated top-down view, whole figure and boots visible. CENTER: identical zombie dead, flattened onto its back on the ground, head pointing left and boots right, one arm splayed and the other bent; foreshortened from the same game camera. RIGHT: identical corpse face-down diagonally, head upper right and feet lower left, limbs slack, one knee bent. Retain identical clothing, hair, body size and material colours in every pose. Corpses must read as bodies lying flat, with gravity and overlap, using newly drawn poses. Keep heads and limbs intact, subtle tattered clothing and a few rusty-red pixels, no exposed organs. No floor, shadows, blood pools, text, labels, border, checkerboard, glow, blur or gradients. Restrained original survival-game pixel art; keep pixel scale and character scale consistent across all three poses. Character design:

pose_character_prompts.commuter: COMMON SHAMBLER / COMMUTER. Adult female zombie with a short black bob, pallid gray skin, dusty teal buttoned cardigan over a gray top, dark plum trousers and charcoal shoes. One shoulder lower, uneven relaxed arms, ordinary human build. Clear silhouette and compact head/body ratio like the approved shambler; individual hairstyle and clothing make this a different common zombie, without adding weapons or accessories.
pose_character_prompts.raincoat: COMMON SHAMBLER / RAINCOAT. Adult balding male zombie, a ragged knee-length faded olive raincoat hanging open over a brown shirt, slate trousers, muddy boots, pale gray-olive skin. One hanging coat panel shorter than the other. Rounded slumped shoulders, slack head tilted to one side. The coat hem gives this ordinary zombie a distinct silhouette from the short-shirt and cardigan variants.
pose_character_prompts.stalker: SPECIAL ZOMBIE / STALKER. A lean gaunt adult infected, long narrow arms held low, deeply hunched forward shoulders, small tucked neck, wary lowered head and thin legs. Faded ash-gray torn shirt, charcoal narrow trousers, pale cool gray skin, sparse dark hair. Compact large-head game proportions still match the references, but a narrow bent silhouette should distinguish the stalker from a normal shambler; no weapons, powers, giant claws or fantasy spikes.
pose_character_prompts.runner: SPECIAL ZOMBIE / RUNNER. A wiry adult infected in a torn muted rust-red athletic top, graphite shorts or narrow trousers and worn dark running shoes, short cropped hair, pale grey skin. Living pose is a low forward poised crouch, knees bent and elbows drawn back, one foot ahead, visibly ready to sprint. This is a distinct kinetic silhouette, keeping reference head scale and chunky pixel construction. Corpse poses keep the rust-red top, thin athletic build and shoes.
pose_character_prompts.armored: SPECIAL ZOMBIE / ARMORED, assembled character design study. Adult stocky infected with a battered dull slate protective helmet, worn dark olive plate vest over a torn tan shirt, heavy charcoal trousers and boots, pale grey face and bare forearms. Armor reads as broad simple hard blocks, not intricate military equipment; nothing held in hands, no logos, no insignia. Upright heavy slouch with wide squared shoulders and an exposed tilted face. The same helmet and vest remain identifiable on both fallen poses. This is a composed visual study; wearable layers will be separated for the game later.
pose_character_prompts.heavy: SPECIAL ZOMBIE / HEAVY. A massive broad adult infected whose body is visibly about a third wider and somewhat taller than the common zombie, very thick shoulders and forearms, powerful heavy legs, a small-looking head sunk between the shoulders. Pale desaturated gray-olive skin, a stretched torn dark brown work vest or sleeveless shirt, bulky slate work trousers and boots. Distinguish by dense muscle and a square loaded silhouette rather than a round swollen stomach; no spikes, weapons or fantasy mutations. Fallen poses keep the unmistakable large mass and thick limbs.

human_initial_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: simplyZOMBIES human corpse pose sheet for visual review and sprite extraction. The reference image is the approved human survivor base. Preserve that exact compact game-art design: warm tan skin, simple brown cropped hair, sleeveless warm tan/brown basic underclothes, short dark trousers and dark boots, no armor, helmet, backpack or held weapon. Same chunky enlarged native 32-pixel sprite aesthetic, large simple head, short limbs, dark stepped outline, broad pixel clusters, only 3–4 flat tones per material, upper-left light. Exactly FOUR isolated static corpse poses in a roomy 2 by 2 arrangement on true RGBA transparency; no living standing pose. Top-left: face-up, head left and feet right, arms relaxed unevenly, one knee slightly bent. Top-right: face-down, head toward upper-right and boots lower-left, arms spread loosely. Bottom-left: resting on left side, head toward upper-left, knees drawn in slightly, one forearm beneath torso. Bottom-right: face-up diagonal opposite to the top-right body, head lower-left and feet upper-right, one arm overhead and one beside the body. Every pose must clearly show a dead adult body lying flat on the ground from the same elevated top-down three-quarter game camera, with new anatomy, gravity, foreshortening and overlapping limbs. Whole bodies, feet and hands visible inside their separate cells. Keep the same head, clothes and proportions in all four. No injuries, gore, exposed organs, blood pool, shadows, floor, scenery, labels, letters, numbers, frame, checkerboard, glow, smooth gradient or blur. Do not add equipment; the game's wearable layers are separate. Static poses only; not a death animation sequence.
human_cleanup_attempts: Edit the attached four-pose pixel-art human corpse sheet. Preserve exactly the four body poses, clothing, proportions, colors and pixel shapes. Remove the entire brown/orange halo, glow, vignette, shadow and all background around every body. Background must be truly transparent RGBA, right up to the hard dark pixel silhouette. Keep body pixels opaque. No floor, no black backdrop, no checkerboard, no shadow. Do not rearrange the four bodies. Only the four isolated clean pixel-art bodies should remain on transparency.
Remove the background, shadows, and brown glow around the four pixel-art bodies. Keep only the four bodies with hard crisp edges, fully opaque on true transparent background.

animation_sources.prompt:
Create a production-oriented sprite animation sheet for simplyZOMBIES, derived from the attached single standing character. Preserve this exact zombie's silhouette, head, outfit, torn fabric, colors and chunky pixel-art construction. Original compact survival-game pixel art, elevated top-down three-quarter camera, strong dark stepped outline, broad discrete pixel clusters, only 3–4 flat colors per material. NO soft shading or painterly gradients. Restrained olive, ochre, slate palette.

EXACT LAYOUT: 20 complete small character sprites in a regular 5-column by 4-row grid. Each cell same size. Large clean TRANSPARENT gutters. No labels, letters, numbers, arrows, grid lines or floor. Entire canvas true RGBA transparency. No glow, shadow, blur, checkerboard or ground plane. Every character comfortably fits inside its cell with visible boots; all figures have identical scale and head size.

ROW 1: facing SOUTH toward viewer, elevated camera.
ROW 2: facing EAST to viewer's right, elevated side view.
ROW 3: facing NORTH away from viewer, showing back of head and back of clothes.
ROW 4: facing WEST to viewer's left, elevated side view; draw the actual other side of the same asymmetric clothing, not a mirrored east row.
Every row: COLUMN 1 is neutral idle stance. COLUMNS 2–5 are FOUR ordered WALK CYCLE frames that loop 2→3→4→5→2:
col2 left leg extended forward, right leg back, opposite arms counter-swing.
col3 weight passes over left supporting leg, right knee bent moving forward; arms pass body.
col4 right leg extended forward, left leg back, opposite arms counter-swing.
col5 weight passes over right supporting leg, left knee bent moving forward; arms pass body.
Clearly different leg/arm geometry in all four frames. Walk IN PLACE with stable body center and shared contact baseline, no drifting across cells. Subtle one-pixel torso bob is okay; head/outfit must not morph or change size. No duplicated still poses, no rotating a single image. Keep the torso posture characteristic of the reference, use the compact proportions and pixel scale in the source. South/east/north/west row ordering and five columns are essential.

Character and movement: Ochre torn shirt, gray trousers, brown boots and brown side-part hair. Ordinary common shambler. Slow uneven shambling gait, loose hanging arms swing slightly, knees bend while one foot drags briefly. Do draw the prescribed four distinct alternating phases, with all four directions.
